clue.text: Uninspiring President sadly adopting leadership of America

indicators.note: adopting means the shuffled letters take in another piece
sadly suggests the word President has come to grief, so its letters are rearranged
leadership of a word is its leading letter, taken from America

explanation.surface: A dull head of state, made duller by taking charge of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges PRESIDENT; 'adopting' puts the A that 'leadership of America' gives inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and lacking imagination, a close synonym of uninspiring.

clue.text: Central item removed from verses in garland

indicators.note: the central item of the five-letter word is the middle letter, which is taken out

parts.note: poesy is an old word for poetry, verses collectively

explanation.surface: Someone stripping the middle line out of a poem written into a floral wreath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central item removed from' takes the middle E out of POESY.
explanation.definitionFit: A posy is a small bunch of flowers, close kin to a garland or wreath of blooms.

clue.text: Desperate? Access given to most of quantity of food

parts.note: a door is a means of access

indicators.note: most of a word drops its last letter

parts.note: a diet is the food a person regularly eats

explanation.surface: Someone frantic for food finally gets let in to the larder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims DIET to DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-or-die attempt is a desperate, all-or-nothing one.

clue.text: Wind a beauty? One blows over a basket

parts.note: to snake is to wind or twist along
a charmer is an attractive, captivating person

explanation.surface: Is a breezy person a beauty? A cryptic riddle about someone playing over a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as air, but is the verb, to snake. The definition paints the snake charmer piping over a basket of snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake charmer plays a pipe over a basket from which a cobra rises.

clue.text: Supports (one heard) non-alcoholic drink

parts.note: a root is what supports and anchors a plant

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: one of the supports, a bier, the stand that supports a coffin

explanation.surface: A bracketed aside about props, followed by a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supports' gives two things: a ROOT and a BIER, the second ('one') turned by 'heard' into its sound-alike BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Root beer is a sweet American soft drink flavoured with sassafras root, containing no alcohol.

clue.text: A change required around island feature of zoo

indicators.note: around means the word for change goes round the island letter

parts.note: to vary is to change

explanation.surface: A zoo needs remodelling around its island enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a large enclosure for birds, a standard attraction at a zoo.

clue.text: Foundation dismissing current singer

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a basis is a foundation
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A building foundation laid without any electrical supply, alongside a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass is a singer with the lowest male voice.

clue.text: Studio more impressive but not quiet

indicators.note: not here signals that the letters for quiet are left out

parts.note: statelier means grander, more impressive
st is a hushing call, a demand for quiet

explanation.surface: A studio that is grander than others, but noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'st!' is an old interjection asking for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop, i.e. a studio.

clue.text: Arctic vehicle is blown off-course around second ridge, finally

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go round the word for second
off-course suggests the letters have strayed, so they are rearranged

parts.note: mo is a short moment, a second

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of ridge

explanation.surface: A polar vehicle is pushed off its route by the wind around a mountain ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-course' rearranges IS BLOWN to SNOWBIL; 'around' places MO inside it, and 'finally' adds the E ending ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowmobile is a motor vehicle on skis or tracks used in polar regions.

clue.text: One suffers with no chance of treatment in store

definitions.text: One suffers with no chance of treatment in store

parts.words: One suffers with no chance of treatment in store
parts.note: reads as a patient with an incurable illness, but it is a compulsive buyer whose condition is 'treated' only in a shop

explanation.surface: A patient faces an illness with no hope of a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in store' seems to mean 'awaiting', but it is literal: the sufferer's affliction lives in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopaholic is a person addicted to shopping, an affliction indulged in stores.

clue.text: Leave service, after Bishop fails to appear for the presentation

indicators.note: fails to appear means the bishop letter is absent

parts.note: to demob is to be released from military service
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman skips a church service and misses a presentation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests church, near 'Bishop', but it is military service.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a demonstration, a presentation showing how something works.

clue.text: Fielder about to secure wicket? This one's waiting for the right moment

definitions.text: This one's waiting for the right moment

indicators.note: about means the fielder's word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a catcher is a fielder, in baseball or cricket
to lock is to secure
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder poised to clinch a wicket, waiting for the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket scene suggests patience, but the definition is a bored worker eyeing the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock-watcher is a worker who keeps checking the time, waiting for the moment to stop.

clue.text: Curtailed suggestion about pound in vain

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes round the pound letter
curtailed means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: an idea is a suggestion
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A short proposal about money comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailed' cuts IDEA to IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean futile or without effect, as in idle threats, so it matches vain.

clue.text: Be unfortunate, keeping very ill, not very doddery

indicators.note: keeping means the word for unfortunate holds the other letters

parts.note: bum as an adjective means bad or unlucky, as in a bum deal

indicators.note: doddery means shaky and unsteady, so the letters are rearranged
not means the letter for very is left out

explanation.surface: Someone told to be unlucky while caring for a very sick, shaky old person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' is not a verb but the chemical symbol. 'not very' drops V from VERY ILL; 'doddery' rearranges ERYILL to ERYLLI, which 'keeping' places inside BUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Be is the chemical symbol for the element beryllium, a crossword-only style of definition.

clue.text: Face doubts uncertainly, becoming confused

indicators.note: uncertainly suggests the letters are unsettled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone facing doubts in a wavering way and growing muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Obfuscated means made obscure or unclear, so muddled or confused.

clue.text: Comrades, trio, cut down, cornered by gun

indicators.note: cornered by means the gun's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: the Bren is a British light machine gun

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: a trio is three

explanation.surface: Three comrades are shot down when trapped by a gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' trims THREE to THRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Brethren is an old plural of brother, used for fellow members or comrades.

clue.text: Symbol of Egypt that is resident in Egypt?

parts.note: sc. is the abbreviation of Latin scilicet, meaning that is to say
an Arab is a typical resident of Egypt

explanation.surface: Asking whether an emblem of Egypt is really a local inhabitant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' looks like a link but gives SC, as 'i.e.' might.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab beetle was sacred in ancient Egypt and is a widely used Egyptian emblem.

clue.text: Criminal staying in party with free food to the end?

indicators.note: staying in means the criminal's word sits inside the party word

parts.note: a lig is British slang for a party or event with free food and drink
a felon is a criminal

explanation.surface: A crook freeloading at a party with a free buffet, staying until the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: LIG, a freeloader's party in British slang, is not well known outside Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifelong means lasting through one's whole life, right up to the end.

clue.text: Tentative jokes, lacking power — clean, but lacking power

indicators.note: lacking means the power letter is taken away

parts.note: puns are jokes

indicators.note: lacking again means the power letter is dropped

parts.note: pure means clean

explanation.surface: A hesitant comic with weak gags, wholesome but limp.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces lose a P: PUNS becomes UNS and PURE becomes URE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsure means hesitant and lacking confidence, which is tentative.

clue.text: Tiny cut in stone — small piece cut out

indicators.note: in means the shortened word goes inside the stone letters

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tiny is a small child, as is a nipper

explanation.surface: A tiny nick in a stone, as a little piece is chipped away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiny' is a noun, a small child; 'cut' trims NIPPER to NIPPE. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece snipped or extracted from something larger.

clue.text: Significant figure part of Victorian bicycle design?

definitions.meaning: the penny-farthing bicycle had one large front wheel

explanation.surface: An important person spotted in an old bicycle's design.
explanation.definitionFit: Big wheel is an idiom for a bigwig, and the penny-farthing's front wheel was literally big.

clue.text: Use up a metal dividing bar, trimming volume

indicators.note: dividing means the other pieces split the shortened word
trimming means the volume letter is cut away

parts.note: to veto is to bar
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Using up a metal ingot as a divider while shaving down its volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' reads as a metal ingot but is the verb, to forbid; 'trimming volume' shortens it before 'dividing' sends the metal phrase through it.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into resources is to consume or use them up gradually.

clue.text: Brief film about whiskey

indicators.note: about means the film word goes round the other letter

parts.note: a film is a thin layer
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A short movie about a whiskey distillery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective for the film but is a noun: a barrister's slang name.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is informal for a lawyer, especially a defence counsel.

clue.text: I whine when engaging in dream of bad behaviour?

indicators.note: engaging in means the inner pieces are taken inside the other word

parts.note: to dream of something is to crave it
a mew is a thin whining cry

explanation.surface: Someone moaning whenever they fantasise about misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whine' is a cat's thin cry, not a complaint; 'engaging in' sets that cry, after I, inside the word for longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime wave is a sudden rise in lawbreaking, bad behaviour on a large scale.

clue.text: Time and again leading articles will offer valediction

indicators.note: again means the pair is used a second time
leading points to the front letter of the word

explanation.surface: Newspaper leaders repeatedly signing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' gives T and 'leading' gives A from articles; 'again' doubles the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British farewell, and a valediction is a goodbye.

clue.text: Scrutinises base for sure

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
sure as a reply means yes

explanation.surface: An inspector examines the foundation to be certain.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it carefully, to scrutinise it.

clue.text: Recording to draw upon energy

indicators.note: upon means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to tap a source is to draw from it
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A recording made to draw on reserves of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape is a magnetic recording, as in a tape of an interview.

clue.text: Auditor's no longer prepared to imagine servility

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the words are taken as they sound

parts.note: being sick of something means being no longer prepared to put up with it, and to fancy is to imagine

explanation.surface: An accountant is tired of fantasising about grovelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant but means a listener: 'sick of fancy' said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophancy is fawning, obsequious flattery, which is servility.

clue.text: Neglected to overlook second requirement

indicators.note: to overlook means to miss out, so the second letter is dropped

parts.note: something dusty has been neglected

explanation.surface: Someone forgot to look over an additional requirement.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty is an obligation, something required of a person.

clue.text: Endless complaint about revolutionary tumult, one engaging lots of people

indicators.note: about means the shortened complaint goes round the other pieces
endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a grouse is a complaint

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: rage, a violent fury, is a tumult
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Constant moaning about revolutionary unrest, from someone who draws in crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts GROUSE to GROUS; 'revolutionary' turns RAGE to EGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregarious means sociable, fond of company and mixing with many others.
